For our client's protection, no account flag against the driver is warranted on these facts: the driver did press or fire a false "I'm Here" (F4) and the two prior no-show disputes upheld on his profile (F15) are profile history only, which the policy says cannot decide the case and, on the current record, are the only adverse data points.

events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.95)
events.body:
The rider cancelled, so NS-0 sends the case to the rider-cancellation rule: NS-4. The timeline shows acceptance at 18:23:00 and rider cancellation at 18:25:30, i.e. 2 min 30 s (150 s) after matching — inside the 3-minute window — so no cancellation fee is chargeable at all [F2][NS-4]. The trace's own ✗ on NS-4's "more than 3 min after matching" confirms this.

The $6.61 fee on record therefore fails its only possible basis [F5]. The no-show branch of NS-0 (via NS-1) cannot rescue it: the driver never tapped "I'm Here" (driver_pressed_here_at is null) [F4], the platform never recorded him at the pickup point (driver_arrived_at is null) [F3], and his closest approach was 1806 m, never inside the 200 m radius [F1] — so NS-1 (i) and (ii) both fail, which under NS-2 makes the $6.61 fully refundable [NS-1][NS-2]. No surge applies, so the refundable sum is exactly the fee charged: $6.61 × 1.0× = $6.61 [F5][F6][NS-2].

The driver's "traffic" explanation does not change this: the only traffic record is Boon Lay Way in speed band 3 (20–29 km/h) with no incidents and fair weather, which is not the band 1–2 severe congestion RD-4 recognises, and in any event traffic excuses routing, not a failure of the NS-1 arrival requirements [F11][F12][F13][RD-4][NS-1]. The driver's post-trip statement that he "was on my way" is a statement contradicted by the GPS/timeline records (F1, F3, F4) and cannot support a no-show charge [F10][NS-1][NS-2]; the driver's own 18:24 chat "About 5 min, traffic" likewise shows he had not arrived [F8][NS-1]. Timeliness is satisfied — the cancellation is dated in the timeline and the rider has 0 prior disputes — so NS-7's 30-day window is met and the refund is payable as a voucher [F2][F14][NS-7].

On the safety screen: I read every chat message, the driver's statement and the complaint [F7][F8][F10]. The messages are a neutral ETA inquiry and a neutral ETA reply; the statement is a factual assertion; the complaint is a fee grievance ("the driver was nowhere near"). Nothing contains a threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation [F7][F8][F10][SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. safety_concern = none.

No account flag is warranted: NS-2 attaches a flag only where the driver pressed "I'm Here" while GPS placed him away from the pickup (tl-here has a value and within_200m is false), and F4 shows no such tap was ever recorded [F4][NS-2]. His 90-day profile of 2 upheld no-show disputes is profile history, which cannot decide this case; RD-6's flag is tied to a route-deviation finding that does not arise here [F15][RD-6].

ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7); no account flag against the driver on this record — the prior upheld no-show disputes stay on file for any future review.
ruling.reasoning:
The rider cancelled, so NS-0 sends the case to the rider-cancellation rule: NS-4. The timeline shows acceptance at 18:23:00 and rider cancellation at 18:25:30, i.e. 2 min 30 s (150 s) after matching — inside the 3-minute window — so no cancellation fee is chargeable at all [F2][NS-4]. The trace's own ✗ on NS-4's "more than 3 min after matching" confirms this.

The $6.61 fee on record therefore fails its only possible basis [F5]. The no-show branch of NS-0 (via NS-1) cannot rescue it: the driver never tapped "I'm Here" (driver_pressed_here_at is null) [F4], the platform never recorded him at the pickup point (driver_arrived_at is null) [F3], and his closest approach was 1806 m, never inside the 200 m radius [F1] — so NS-1 (i) and (ii) both fail, which under NS-2 makes the $6.61 fully refundable [NS-1][NS-2]. Nothing contains a threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation [F7][F8][F10][SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. safety_concern = none.

Not rejected in outcome but the RD-4 framing is inapplicable as a defence for the driver: F11 shows only band 3 (20–29 km/h) with no incident [F12] and fair weather [F13], and RD-4 excuses routing rather than the NS-1 arrival failure shown by F1/F3/F4. The point is noted only to show traffic does not assist the driver.

Accepted only insofar as no flag is warranted; the assertion that the driver 'did press or fire a false I'm Here' is contradicted by F4 (driver_pressed_here_at is null), and NS-2's flag trigger therefore fails on the record.

claims.assertion: The driver never reached the pickup point: his closest recorded approach was 1806 m at 18:25:30, and the platform never recorded him at the pickup point (driver_arrived_at is null).
The driver never tapped "I'm Here", so the first requirement for a no-show cancellation fee (NS-1 (i)) fails and the fee cannot stand.

Because the driver was never within 200 m of the pickup point, the NS-1 (ii) GPS-location requirement is unsatisfied, so $6.61 must be refunded in full; the $6.61 cancellation fee is confirmed on record and no surge applied.
The rider cancelled 2 min 30 s after acceptance, within Ryde's 3-minute no-charge window, so no cancellation fee was chargeable in the first place.
The driver's own message at 18:24 said he was still "About 5 min" away, which is consistent with the GPS record that he was never near the pickup point and leaves no basis for a no-show fee.

The driver's post-trip statement "I was on my way when the rider cancelled" concedes he had not arrived, and traffic cannot excuse non-arrival: the only recorded condition was Boon Lay Way at 20-29 km/h (band 3) with no incidents and fair weather.
The driver's account shows 2 no-show disputes upheld in the last 90 days, so this repeat pattern of unfulfilled arrival claims supports flagging the account for Ryde review alongside the refund.
The complaint was filed on the rider's 604-day account with 0 prior disputes within the 30-day dispute window, so the refund is timely.

weaknesses: The rider is the cancelling party, so the driver may argue the $6.61 fee is owed under the general cancellation rule (NS-0 / NS-4) if the 3-minute threshold is read strictly: F2 shows cancellation at 18:25:30, exactly 2 min 30 s after acceptance, which actually supports us, but the rider's own complaint that she 'cancelled within 2 minutes' slightly overstates the timing.

The driver's written statement F10 ('I was on my way when the rider cancelled') is the other side's main evidence, though it is unsupported by F1 (never within 200 m) and F4 (no 'I'm Here' tap), so it loses to the system records.

F11 shows mild congestion (band 3) on Boon Lay Way, which the driver may cite as a travel delay, although F12 records no incidents and band 3 is far above the severe-congestion bands (1-2) that could justify a delay defence.

Nothing in the record shows the driver's ETA was breached in-app (no ETA field, per NS-8 being informational), so our C4 timing argument rests on the record fee and the 3-minute rule rather than any delay-based waiver.

claims.assertion: This is an instant booking cancelled by the rider 2 min 30 s after acceptance (F2), i.e. within the 3-minute grace window, so under NS-4 no cancellation fee is chargeable at all and the $6.61 on record (F5) must be refunded in full.

The charge cannot alternatively be justified under the no-show branch: NS-1 requires the driver to have pressed "I'm Here", but the platform shows driver_pressed_here_at is null (F4), the driver never entered the 200 m pickup radius (closest approach 1806 m at 18:25:30, F1), and driver_arrived_at is null (F3).

Because NS-1 (i)-(iii) all fail, NS-2 governs: the $6.61 cancellation fee must be refunded in full, and that refund amount is confirmed by the fare record showing the fee charged (F5, with no surge component per F6).

Nothing in the chat supports a no-show: the rider asked for an ETA at 18:23 (F7) and the driver answered "About 5 min, traffic" at 18:24 (F8) — i.e. the driver himself indicated he had not yet arrived when the rider cancelled — and the driver's only other statement is that he was still on his way (F10).

The driver's "traffic" explanation does not convert a rider cancellation into a chargeable no-show: the only traffic record is BOON LAY WAY speed band 3 (20–29 km/h, F11), which is not even band 1 or 2 and, in any event, traffic evidence under RD-4 excuses routing, not the failure of the NS-1 arrival requirements (F1, F3, F4).

For our client's protection, no account flag against the driver is warranted on these facts: the driver did press or fire a false "I'm Here" (F4) and the two prior no-show disputes upheld on his profile (F15) are profile history only, which the policy says cannot decide the case and, on the current record, are the only adverse data points.

weaknesses: F1 and F3 are the rider's strongest cards: the closest GPS approach was 1806 m and driver_arrived_at is null, which directly establishes the NS-1 (ii) element is unmet and leaves no room to argue the driver was "at the pick-up location" — my strongest route is therefore to concede the refund and save the account, not to resist the $6.61.

F15 shows 2 disputes and 2 upheld no-show disputes on the driver's 90-day profile (777 trips); while RD-6 requires an upheld case in this case to trigger a flag and no_show flags are not the route-deviation flag, this history is the fact the other side will use to argue a pattern of cancellation/waiting-button abuse (NS-2, A10 context), and I cannot rebut it from the fact table.

F11 (band 3, 20–29 km/h on Boon Lay Way during 18:18–18:30) plus F10 ("I was on my way") is the only material the driver has to explain the 1806 m distance, and it falls short of the RD-4 "reasonable cause" standard (no incident record, F12; no band 1/2), so the traffic excuse is likely to be rejected rather than accepted.

If the judge treats dispute B-0029 as a completed-trip waiting-fee matter rather than a rider cancellation, NS-6 could be in play instead of NS-4; the timeline shows no trip completion and no rider boarding (F2, F3), but that reading would still end in a full reversal against the driver.

points.response: Agreed on the outcome: cancellation 2 min 30 s after acceptance (F2) is inside the 3-minute grace window, so the $6.61 on record (F5) is not chargeable — my client asks for exactly this full refund.

Concurred and it is the core of my case: the driver never tapped "I'm Here" (F4), never entered the pickup radius — closest approach 1806 m (F1) — and driver_arrived_at is null (F3), so NS-1 (i)-(iii) all fail.
Agreed: NS-2 applies, the $6.61 is refunded in full, and the amount is fixed by the fare record with no surge component (F5, F6).

Agreed and I adopt it: the driver's own 18:24 message "About 5 min, traffic" (F8) shows he had not arrived, and his post-trip statement that he was "on my way" (F10) is a claim contradicted by the GPS record (F1), so it cannot support a no-show charge.

Agreed that traffic does not help the driver: only Boon Lay Way band 3, 20-29 km/h, is recorded (F11), with no incidents and fair weather (F12, F13), and band 3 is not the band 1-2 severe congestion RD-4 recognises; and in any event traffic cannot satisfy the NS-1 arrival requirements (F1, F3, F4).

Contested: I do not ask for a flag as the main remedy, but the driver's profile of 2 no-show disputes, 2 upheld in 90 d (F15) is a legitimate supporting basis for sending the account for Ryde review of unfulfilled arrival claims, and the flag is only an adjunct to the full refund, never the finding; my claim C7 rests on F15 for that purpose only.

Conceded: the system record is unambiguous that the driver's closest approach was 1806 m at 18:25:30 and that driver_arrived_at is null, so there is no factual base to dispute non-arrival and no argument in our favour on NS-1 (ii).
Conceded: driver_pressed_here_at is null, so NS-1 (i) fails outright and the no-show route to a $6.61 fee is closed to the rider's side and unavailable to us.

Conceded: with NS-1 (i)-(iii) unmet, NS-2 makes the $6.61 refundable in full, and the refund figure of $6.61 is directly computable from the fare record (no surge under F6) — this is exactly the outcome we requested, so there is nothing left to argue about quantum.

We do not contest the arithmetic: acceptance 18:23:00 to cancellation 18:25:30 is 2 min 30 s (F2), inside the 3-minute window, so NS-4 independently bars any fee; the rider's complaint wording ('within 2 minutes') is imprecise but immaterial because the system timestamp controls.

Conceded: the driver's own 18:24 message "About 5 min, traffic" (F8) is inconsistent with any claim of having arrived, and read against F1 it simply confirms he was still en route; we do not build anything on it.

Conceded on liability: F10 is a statement, not consent or proof of arrival, and it loses to the GPS/timeline records (F1, F3, F4); the traffic material helps us even less, since F11 is only band 3 (20-29 km/h), F12 records no incident, and F13 records fair weather, so there is no RD-4-style reasonable cause and no traffic exemption to claim.

We contest the flag: no flag of any kind is triggered here, because NS-2 attaches a flag only where the driver actually pressed "I'm Here" while GPS placed him elsewhere (tl-here has a value and within_200m is false), and F4 shows no such tap was ever recorded; the 2 upheld no-show disputes in F15 are profile history (2 of 777 trips) which by rule cannot decide this case and do not support an abuse finding on F1/F3/F4, and NS-6 — a waiting-fee clause with no application to a rider cancellation — cannot be the basis for a flag either.

We do not contest timeliness: the cancellation is dated in the timeline record (F2) and the rider's account history (F14) shows no prior fee disputes, so NS-7's 30-day window is satisfied and the refund is payable in voucher form.
